content: 1. Mifepristone increases the levels or effects of ribociclib by inhibiting the metabolism of the hepatic/intestinal enzyme CYP3A4. Both ribociclib and mifepristone prolong the QTc interval. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. Monitor closely if coadministration is necessary. 2. Rifabutin decreases the levels or effects of mifepristone by inducing the metabolism of the hepatic/intestinal enzyme CYP3A4. Use caution and monitor closely. Coadministration with CYP3A4 inducers is not recommended as per the manufacturer. 3. Mifepristone increases the levels or effects of rifabutin by inhibiting the metabolism of the hepatic/intestinal enzyme CYP3A4. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. Monitor closely if coadministration is necessary. 4. Rifampin decreases the levels or effects of mifepristone by inducing the metabolism of the hepatic/intestinal enzyme CYP3A4. Use caution and monitor closely. Coadministration with CYP3A4 inducers is not recommended as per the manufacturer. 5. Mifepristone increases the levels or effects of rifampin by inhibiting the metabolism of the hepatic/intestinal enzyme CYP3A4. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. Monitor closely if coadministration is necessary. 6. Rifapentine decreases the levels or effects of mifepristone by inducing the metabolism of the hepatic/intestinal enzyme CYP3A4. Use caution and monitor closely. Coadministration with CYP3A4 inducers is not recommended as per the manufacturer. 7. Mifepristone increases the levels or effects of rifapentine by inhibiting the metabolism of the hepatic/intestinal enzyme CYP3A4. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. Monitor closely if coadministration is necessary. 8. Mifepristone increases the levels or effects of rimegepant by inhibiting the metabolism of the hepatic/intestinal enzyme CYP3A4. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. 9. Mifepristone increases the levels or effects of riociguat by decreasing its metabolism. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. Monitor for signs of hypotension and reduce the dose of riociguat if needed. 10. Mifepristone increases the levels or effects of ripretinib by inhibiting the metabolism of the hepatic/intestinal enzyme CYP3A4. Use caution and monitor closely. Coadministration with strong CYP3A inhibitors increases systemic exposure to ripretinib and its active metabolite (DP-5439), which may increase the risk of adverse reactions. 11. Mifepristone and risperidone both prolong the QTc interval. Modify therapy or monitor closely. Use alternatives if available. 12. Ritonavir increases the levels or effects of mifepristone by inhibiting the metabolism of the hepatic/intestinal enzyme CYP3A4. Use caution and monitor closely. Do not exceed 300 mg/day of mifepristone for Cushing syndrome when coadministered with strong CYP3A4 inhibitors. 13. Mifepristone increases the levels or effects of ritonavir by inhibiting the metabolism of the hepatic/intestinal enzyme CYP3A4. Modify therapy or monitor closely. 14. Mifepristone increases the toxicity of rivaroxaban by enhancing anticoagulation. Monitor closely. Mifepristone also increases the levels or effects of rivaroxaban by inhibiting the metabolism of the hepatic/intestinal enzyme CYP3A4. Modify therapy or monitor closely. 15. Mifepristone increases the levels or effects of roflumilast topical by inhibiting the metabolism of the hepatic/intestinal enzyme CYP3A4. Use caution and monitor closely. 16. Mifepristone and romidepsin both prolong the QTc interval. Modify therapy or monitor closely. Use alternatives if available. 17. Mifepristone increases the levels or effects of romidepsin by inhibiting the metabolism of the hepatic/intestinal enzyme CYP3A4. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. 18. Mifepristone increases the levels or effects of rosiglitazone by inhibiting CYP2C8/2C9. Use the smallest recommended doses for substrates and monitor closely. 19. Mifepristone increases the toxicity of rosuvastatin by mechanisms other than CYP3A4 inhibition. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. 20. Rucaparib increases the levels or effects of mifepristone by inhibiting the metabolism of the hepatic/intestinal enzyme CYP3A4. Modify therapy or monitor closely. Adjust the dosage of CYP3A4 substrates if clinically indicated. 21. Mifepristone increases the levels or effects of ruxolitinib by inhibiting the metabolism of the hepatic/intestinal enzyme CYP3A4. The clinical significance of this interaction is unknown. 22. Mifepristone increases the levels or effects of sacubitril/valsartan by mechanisms other than CYP3A4 inhibition. Use caution and monitor closely. Valsartan is a substrate of the hepatic uptake transporter OATP1B1, and coadministration with OATP1B1 inhibitors may increase valsartan systemic exposure. 23. Mifepristone increases the levels or effects of salmeterol by inhibiting the metabolism of the hepatic/intestinal enzyme CYP3A4. Use caution and monitor closely. 24. Mifepristone increases the levels or effects of saxagliptin by inhibiting the metabolism of the hepatic/intestinal enzyme CYP3A4. Modify therapy or monitor closely. 25. Mifepristone decreases the effects of segesterone/ethinyl estradiol by pharmacodynamic antagonism. Use caution and monitor closely. A backup contraceptive method is recommended. 26. Mifepristone increases the levels of seladelpar by inhibiting the metabolism of the hepatic/intestinal enzyme CYP3A4. Use caution and monitor closely. Exercise caution in patients who are poor CYP2C9 metabolizers and are coadministered a moderate/strong CYP3A4 inhibitor. 27. Mifepristone increases the levels or effects of selegiline by mechanisms other than CYP3A4 inhibition. Use caution and monitor closely.
